standing: Proposed local carrier design and future fault-injection plan; not public wire schema, executable storage, crash test results or independent acceptance. Extended by the carrierFormat 3 correction with cases F38-F48; every added case is not-executed.

recordSchema.description: Constant 1; reject unknown versions before joins.

storeGenerationDigest.description: SHA-256 of exact canonical private StoreGenerationBindingV1; compare with the custody-admitted active or explicitly selected historical store generation.

namespaceId.description: Exact receipt namespace and registered project namespace; binary equality, no path resolution.

executionId.description: Exact host attempt ExecutionId and receipt executionId; never derived from operationRef.

runId.description: Byte-equal evaluator RunId, SEAL runId and receipt runId; current run3 only.

inventoryDigest.description: Exact admitted retention inventory and receipt inventoryDigest.

commitSequence.description: Canonical decimal text for receipt commitSequence 0..18446744073709551615; parse as an exact integer, never SQL REAL or JavaScript Number.

receiptBytesSha256.description: Raw SHA-256 of the exact stored receipt bytes; verify its selected schema and signer/custody separately.

journalCarrierDigest.description: Existing journal projectKeyDigest from the security-owned carrier binding, not a hash of a caller-supplied path.

grantGeneration.description: Exact positive i64 security generation; inherited metadata range.

journalSeq.description: Exact ordinary-append sequence; inherited uint53 terminal slot 9007199254740991 stays reserved even though the broader product record shape permits i64.

journalBodySha256.description: Exact security carrier body hash of the validated SEAL; verify the owner hash chain and witness, not only this string.

operationRef.description: Exact security-owned op- plus 32 lowercase hex token from the live session; map explicitly to executionId without changing either grammar.

extraAdmissionRules: commitSequence must decode exactly to uint64; length/pattern alone does not enforce the upper bound.
JSON booleans are not integers; unknown fields, duplicate keys and lossy numeric parsing are refused.
All exact owner joins and witness/hash-chain/high-water checks in the owning prose are mandatory.

Private SQL commitSequence is canonical decimal TEXT with binary collation and length 1..20; one private ledger accessor implements length-then-bytes comparison and exact uint64 decoding. No bare lexical MAX/ORDER BY, integer CAST or REAL path may allocate or order commits. The private association mirrors the already allocated receipt counter; it never allocates one.

cases.checkpoint: Before project/store admission
cases.possibleStoredState: No new source-derived state
cases.expectedBehavior: No live writer/session; no commit call; reads for diagnosis remain read-only.

cases.checkpoint: Replay refuses or target/inventory is substituted
cases.possibleStoredState: No authoritative receipt
cases.expectedBehavior: Neither structural-only validation nor a stale boolean/token can publish authority.

cases.checkpoint: During temporary object write
cases.possibleStoredState: Partial private temp files; no ledger receipt
cases.expectedBehavior: Do not expose partial objects; later authorized reconciliation may remove orphans.

cases.checkpoint: After temp write, before file barrier completes
cases.possibleStoredState: Temporary bytes may or may not survive
cases.expectedBehavior: Never infer durability from write return alone.

cases.checkpoint: After object file barrier, during digest-addressed publication
cases.possibleStoredState: Some immutable objects may be present
cases.expectedBehavior: Verify existing collisions by exact digest/length; never overwrite unequal bytes.

cases.checkpoint: After object publication, before directory barrier completes
cases.possibleStoredState: Visible names may not survive restart
cases.expectedBehavior: No receipt has committed; presence alone grants no authority.

cases.checkpoint: After object barriers, journal/evidence transaction acquisition refused or busy
cases.possibleStoredState: Durable orphan objects; no ledger receipt
cases.expectedBehavior: Acquire journal then evidence level-3 transactions before append lock; if either acquisition fails release earlier resources, apply S7 non-waiting rules and preserve orphan status.

cases.checkpoint: After witness PENDING persist, before SEAL journal transaction
cases.possibleStoredState: Witness may lead journal tail by one
cases.expectedBehavior: Read-only diagnosis reports would-REVERT; only authorized lifecycle open reconciles it.

cases.checkpoint: During SEAL journal append before journal commit
cases.possibleStoredState: Journal transaction may abort; witness PENDING
cases.expectedBehavior: No evidence-ledger commit is permitted yet; validate actual journal tail before deciding REVERT/ADVANCE.

cases.checkpoint: SEAL journal commit outcome unknown
cases.possibleStoredState: SEAL may be durable, witness PENDING
cases.expectedBehavior: Provided evidence ledger absence is verified: uncommitted; inability to read it remains indeterminate. Never proceed to evidence commit on an uncertain journal barrier.

cases.checkpoint: SEAL durable, witness COMMITTED update interrupted
cases.possibleStoredState: Journal at PENDING target or finalized witness
cases.expectedBehavior: Read-only diagnosis reports would-ADVANCE where lawful; no evidence commit until witness finalization succeeds.

cases.checkpoint: SEAL/witness durable, evidence ledger rows partially inserted inside transaction
cases.possibleStoredState: SEAL exists; receipt/association not yet committed
cases.expectedBehavior: Atomic transaction exposes all required rows or none; no commit from a lone SEAL.

cases.checkpoint: Evidence ledger commit syscall returns error/connection lost
cases.possibleStoredState: Transaction may have committed or aborted
cases.expectedBehavior: Initial caller outcome durability-undetermined with ExecutionId. Fresh verified lookup may establish committed or uncommitted; no write retry.

cases.checkpoint: Evidence commit observed before all required carrier barriers confirmed
cases.possibleStoredState: Durable result not yet established
cases.expectedBehavior: Do not return PublishedCommit; recovery examines actual committed receipt and barrier/carrier state.

cases.checkpoint: All commit barriers completed, acknowledgement lost
cases.possibleStoredState: Exact receipt and association committed
cases.expectedBehavior: Fresh read-only lookup confirms historical commitment and separately inspects object availability.

cases.checkpoint: Acknowledgement delivered, later process crash
cases.possibleStoredState: Acknowledged sealed history remains
cases.expectedBehavior: Do not re-run mutation or create a second receipt for the same attempt during recovery.

cases.checkpoint: Required projection/HTML/output fails after commit
cases.possibleStoredState: Committed Run remains intact
cases.expectedBehavior: Preserve RunId and existing required-delivery operational failure/exit4.

cases.checkpoint: Optional browser launch/export fails after required delivery
cases.possibleStoredState: Committed Run and required artifact remain
cases.expectedBehavior: Optional effect failure is disclosed without rewriting result or treating export as required.

cases.checkpoint: REV or observer fail-stop before final SEAL checkpoint
cases.possibleStoredState: No later SEAL or evidence commit
cases.expectedBehavior: Disclose already completed external effects under S6; a prior semantic replay token grants no current authority.

cases.checkpoint: Observer stall/freshness failure after SEAL but before evidence commit
cases.possibleStoredState: SEAL may survive; evidence commit prevented if checkpoint fails
cases.expectedBehavior: Recheck after blocking journal/witness work. On failure latch fail-stop, abort evidence transaction, release ordered locks, then record REV through a new lawful journal call; never reacquire level3 under level4. Actual syscall stall bounds require qualification.

cases.checkpoint: Malformed, mismatched or hash-divergent witness
cases.possibleStoredState: Carrier cannot be admitted
cases.expectedBehavior: Quarantine/report the owner condition; never normalize or repair malformed bytes in a read-only query.

cases.checkpoint: Missing witness with a nonempty journal
cases.possibleStoredState: Witnessless restore condition
cases.expectedBehavior: Use security quarantine semantics; a matching SEAL or receipt alone does not bypass custody.

cases.checkpoint: Journal tail below trusted high-water / equal seq different hash
cases.possibleStoredState: Rollback or uncertain tail loss
cases.expectedBehavior: Preserve floors and historical bytes; only owner-authorized recovery can reconcile admitted cases.

cases.checkpoint: Only receipt or only association appears committed
cases.possibleStoredState: Impossible partial transaction or corruption
cases.expectedBehavior: Refuse local commitment confirmation; preserve observed rows for diagnosis, do not synthesize the missing partner.

cases.checkpoint: Evidence ledger unreadable or wrong store selected
cases.possibleStoredState: No reliable lookup conclusion
cases.expectedBehavior: Never interpret failed read, wrong generation or empty fallback DB as no commit.

cases.checkpoint: Confirmed receipt, required evidence later missing/corrupt/purged
cases.possibleStoredState: Historical commitment with changed availability
cases.expectedBehavior: Preserve assurance/verdict; disclose exact missing references and current availability, never reseal.

cases.checkpoint: Revocation or expired grants observed after confirmed commit
cases.possibleStoredState: Historical receipt remains
cases.expectedBehavior: Confirm history without reusing grants for new effects; current custody still gates reading.

cases.checkpoint: Store-generation/namespace/operation/execution binding swap
cases.possibleStoredState: Contradictory local association
cases.expectedBehavior: Refuse substituted recovery target; compare all independent owner joins, not just RunId.

cases.checkpoint: Journal record pruned or unavailable after retained receipt
cases.possibleStoredState: Historical record exists but required recovery custody cannot be reconstructed
cases.expectedBehavior: Never invent a journal proof or erase the historical receipt. Recovery metadata needs a retention root; lawful migrations preserve its verification lineage.

cases.checkpoint: Reader observes transaction during publication
cases.possibleStoredState: Committed snapshot excludes in-flight rows
cases.expectedBehavior: Readers see old complete state or new complete state; no mixed receipt/association. A later valid PENDING journal append does not block confirmation of an earlier durable prefix. A snapshot missing an actively running requested attempt is not final absence.

cases.checkpoint: Competing writer or EXCLUSIVE census while APPEND writer active
cases.possibleStoredState: First admitted writer retains its guard
cases.expectedBehavior: Exercise actual process lock modes and S7 busy/retry behavior; no waiting/upgrades under the wrong lock.

cases.checkpoint: Journal carrier cannot represent schema3 SEAL/current platform
cases.possibleStoredState: Carrier incompatibility detected before commit work
cases.expectedBehavior: Explicit versioned migration required; never insert SEAL into the inherited SQL check set by disabling constraints.

cases.checkpoint: Journal sequence reaches reserved terminal capacity
cases.possibleStoredState: No ordinary SEAL in terminal slot
cases.expectedBehavior: Pause/close generation through the owner lifecycle outside the held operation lease; no fence acquisition or rollover hidden in commit.

cases.checkpoint: Receipt/inventory/signature or journal-body join differs
cases.possibleStoredState: Observed record cannot confirm claimed local commit
cases.expectedBehavior: Hash presence alone is insufficient; validate closed schemas, owner digests, signatures/custody and full object inventory.

cases.checkpoint: Duplicate commit request for the same ExecutionId
cases.possibleStoredState: Existing exact attempt may already be committed
cases.expectedBehavior: Route to read-only recovery; compare requested binding exactly and refuse a different binding; do not INSERT OR REPLACE or auto-append a new SEAL.

cases.checkpoint: Explicit store migration/restore with previous receipt associations
cases.possibleStoredState: Old associations remain tied to old generation
cases.expectedBehavior: Use admitted migration lineage for historical lookup or explicit adoption with a new attempt; never rewrite old association IDs to imply new local authority.

cases.checkpoint: Orphan SEAL followed by a later successful operation
cases.possibleStoredState: An aborted attempt has a valid durable SEAL but no receipt/association; a later attempt commits successfully
cases.expectedBehavior: Keep the earlier SEAL as operational history only. It must never become a committed Run in history, receipt, availability or query selection, including after restart or a later commit in the same journal generation. admit_analysis_seal establishes record and Run validity, not durable commitment; only the guarded evidence-ledger receipt/association establishes that attempt’s commit. A later attempt may lawfully commit the same semantic RunId: report that new ExecutionId/receipt as committed while the earlier ExecutionId remains uncommitted. Never globally blacklist a RunId because one attempt left an orphan SEAL.

cases.checkpoint: Decimal sequence ordering and uint64 conversion boundaries
cases.possibleStoredState: Associations contain exact text values 0, 2, 9, 10, 100 and 18446744073709551615
cases.expectedBehavior: The sole private ordering accessor returns numeric magnitude order and round-trips the full uint64 maximum. Reject leading zeroes, negatives, over-range values and lossy parsing. Exercise the bare lexical MAX/ORDER BY and CAST-to-i64 counterexamples to show why they are forbidden; no allocation decision may use the association column.

cases.checkpoint: Observer latch wins while the attempt state is preparing, after SEAL/witness durable and after association staging
cases.possibleStoredState: Durable SEAL and COMMITTED witness; receipt/association staged but never committed
cases.expectedBehavior: No evidence commit is ever issued. The staged evidence transaction is aborted, level 4 and both level-3 transactions are released, then a fresh lawful level-3 to level-4 append records REV/CLN under the still-held stopped operation lease. The durable SEAL remains an uncommitted attempt exactly as F36 requires and must never become committed history.

cases.checkpoint: Observer latch arrives after the atomic preparing to commit-admitted transition and the commit is later confirmed
cases.possibleStoredState: Exact receipt and association committed and durable
cases.expectedBehavior: The latch cannot undo the syscall or rewrite its outcome. It refuses only subsequent effects. RunId is observable. The gate orders admission only and is not the durability point.

cases.checkpoint: Observer latch arrives after admission, commit confirmed, then required delivery fails
cases.possibleStoredState: Committed Run intact; required artifact not produced
cases.expectedBehavior: Preserve RunId and the existing required-delivery operational failure DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED at exit 4. The latch does not convert a confirmed commit into uncommitted, and delivery failure never rewrites the Run.

cases.checkpoint: Observer latch arrives during the evidence commit syscall and the commit returns an error or a required barrier is unconfirmed
cases.possibleStoredState: Transaction may have committed or aborted
cases.expectedBehavior: Report DURABILITY.COMMIT_FAILED, operational-failed, exit 4. Retain ExecutionId for correlation and omit runId, because RunId is externally observable only for a committed Run. The settled ExecutionId is terminal: no automatic write retry. The latch does not convert this into uncommitted. A later read-only recovery may establish committed or not-committed-verified-absent and may then report the RunId.

cases.checkpoint: Latch and commit admission race at the single atomic attempt state
cases.possibleStoredState: Either no evidence commit was issued, or exactly one was
cases.expectedBehavior: Exactly one of latch-won-preparing and commit-admitted is ever observed. No interleaving may yield both a refusal and a durable commit, and no interleaving may yield uncommitted after a commit syscall was issued. Exercise the real atomic primitive with deterministic synchronisation, not only a model.

cases.checkpoint: mem::forget, process abort or an indefinitely stalled syscall on the commit path
cases.possibleStoredState: Any state; no destructor is guaranteed to have run
cases.expectedBehavior: Drop is best-effort only. These paths must leave recovery evidence and return an honest unavailable or busy result, never a claimed cleanup success. Recovery in a fresh process reads the actual stored bytes and returns a verified conclusion or unknown-custody. No OS cancellation bound may be inferred from Rust types.

cases.checkpoint: Read-only recovery ordering hazard: the association journalSeq exceeds the first observed journal tail
cases.possibleStoredState: Journal read snapshot is older than the evidence ledger snapshot, or the tail was lost
cases.expectedBehavior: Close and reopen the journal read handle exactly once and re-read tail, witness and floor; never re-read the ledger. If reconciled, continue. If still ahead and the SC-TRUST floor lastSeq is at or above the requested sequence, report the F22 quarantine condition. Otherwise return unavailable or busy attributed to the security carrier owner. Never conclude uncommitted, and never draw a conclusion from two different snapshots.

cases.checkpoint: Prefix anchor with a PENDING witness at the next slot and the requested sequence above the SC-TRUST floor
cases.possibleStoredState: Durable prefix exists but no live witnessed anchor names it; a newer append is in flight
cases.expectedBehavior: Report unknown, explicitly not invalidated. The earlier committed receipt is never invalidated by a newer PENDING append. Report the witnessWouldRevert diagnosis and perform no REVERT, no ADVANCE, no witness write and no high-water raise. Do not wait on the writer.

cases.checkpoint: Prefix anchor with a PENDING witness at the tail carrying the tail body hash
cases.possibleStoredState: The append became durable before the witness was advanced
cases.expectedBehavior: The witness still names the durable tail, so it anchors it. Confirm for any requested sequence at or below the tail under anchor class witness-pending-at-tail. Report witnessWouldAdvance as a diagnosis and perform no ADVANCE. The conclusion class is confirmed-under-retained-custody, never cryptographically proven.

cases.checkpoint: The generation holding the requested attempt is carrierFormat 1 or 2
cases.possibleStoredState: Historical generation in which no schema-3 SEAL row can exist
cases.expectedBehavior: Report carrier incompatibility, never not-committed and never uncommitted. Read historical bytes under recordSchema-1 semantics only; never relabel them as schema 3 and never present a historical platform alias as an S8 machine id. This is the read-side counterpart of F31.

cases.checkpoint: Carrier-format migration from 1 or 2 to 3
cases.possibleStoredState: Inherited generation closed by TERMINAL; new carrierFormat 3 objects present
cases.expectedBehavior: TERMINAL closes the inherited generation under the inherited constraints with no constraint or trigger disabled and no row rewritten. The TERMINAL row carries the migration operation own op- token. Inherited rows and inherited schema objects are byte-unchanged and legacy platform aliases are retained verbatim. A second migration aborts. A write to a generation below first_generation is refused. Run the whole transition under the install fence with EXCLUSIVE on the affected namespace and an intent written only after every lease is held.

cases.checkpoint: Post-migration open and read dispatch by a core that does not support carrierFormat 3
cases.possibleStoredState: carrierFormat 3 carrier present
cases.expectedBehavior: A carrierFormat 1-or-2-only core refuses the carrier typed and keeps its prior generation until it expires, mirroring the S9 dual-reader staging. A carrierFormat 1-2-3 core detects the format by schema introspection only, verifies the frozen side-table SQL text byte-equals the frozen definition, verifies the carrier projectKeyDigest and the generation boundary, then reads both historical and current generations without relabelling either.
